$comment: Shared General Provisions. doc "*" means every document draws from these, which is what the Template Details spec calls the shared clause library. Before this, each document carried its own copy — there were three governing-law clauses and two each of notices and entire-agreement, worded differently, with nothing keeping them in agreement. Written once here instead. {{thisDocument}} resolves to the title of whichever document the block is rendering into, which is what lets one piece of text serve all of them.

clauses.title: Governing Law
clauses.rationale: Names the law that applies. Left as a field the user fills in rather than defaulted, because guessing a state for someone is a judgement about their situation.
clauses.body: This {{thisDocument}} is subject to the [[governing law|governing law]] of {{opStateLong}}, without regard to its [[conflict of laws]] principles.

clauses.title: Entire Agreement
clauses.rationale: States that the written document is the whole deal, so earlier drafts and conversations do not become terms.
clauses.body: This {{thisDocument}}, together with its schedules and exhibits, is the entire agreement between the parties on its subject matter and supersedes all prior discussions, proposals, and understandings, whether written or oral.

clauses.title: Amendment
clauses.rationale: Without this, a course of dealing or an email exchange can be argued to have changed the terms.
clauses.body: This {{thisDocument}} may be amended only by a writing signed by each party. No waiver, consent, or course of dealing amends it.

clauses.title: Notices
clauses.rationale: Sets when a notice counts as delivered, which matters whenever a deadline runs from one.
clauses.body: Notices under this {{thisDocument}} shall be in writing and sent to the addresses on the signature page. A notice is deemed given when delivered by hand, one business day after deposit with a national overnight courier, or three business days after deposit in the mail, postage prepaid. Either party may change its address by notice given under this section.

clauses.title: Severability
clauses.rationale: Keeps one unenforceable provision from taking the rest of the document with it.
clauses.body: Under this [[severability|severability]] provision, if any provision of this {{thisDocument}} is held unenforceable, it shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable, or if it cannot be so modified, severed. The remaining provisions continue in full force.

clauses.title: Waiver
clauses.rationale: Not enforcing a right once should not mean giving it up.
clauses.body: No failure or delay in exercising a right under this {{thisDocument}} operates as a waiver of it, and no single or partial exercise precludes any further exercise. A waiver is effective only if in writing and signed by the party granting it.

clauses.title: Assignment
clauses.rationale: Controls whether the counterparty can hand the deal to somebody the other side never agreed to work with.
clauses.body: Neither party may make an [[assignment|assignment]] of this {{thisDocument}} without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, except to a successor in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets. Any purported assignment in breach of this section is void. This {{thisDocument}} binds and benefits the parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

clauses.title: Force Majeure
clauses.rationale: Excuses performance blocked by something neither side controls. The payment carve-out is the point: an inability to pay is not usually treated as force majeure.
clauses.body: Neither party is liable for a delay or failure to perform caused by a [[force majeure]] event beyond its reasonable control, including natural disaster, war, terrorism, civil unrest, labour dispute, epidemic, or failure of a utility or public network. The affected party shall notify the other promptly and resume performance as soon as practicable. This section does not excuse an obligation to pay amounts already due.

clauses.title: Dispute Resolution
clauses.rationale: Escalation and mediation before litigation. Cheaper than the alternative and it does not give up the right to sue.
clauses.body: Before commencing proceedings, the parties shall escalate the dispute to a senior representative of each, who shall confer in good faith for fifteen (15) days. If the dispute is unresolved, the parties shall attempt mediation before a mutually agreed mediator, the cost shared equally. Nothing in this section prevents either party from seeking urgent [[injunctive relief]] at any time.

clauses.title: Limitation of Liability
clauses.rationale: Caps exposure at something proportionate to the deal. The carve-outs are the part people forget: a cap that swallows fraud or a party's own indemnity obligations is unlikely to be given effect and is not usually what either side intended.
clauses.body: Neither party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or for lost profits, revenue, or data, however caused. Each party's total liability arising out of this {{thisDocument}} is limited to the amounts paid or payable under it in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. These limits do not apply to a party's indemnification obligations, to breach of confidentiality, to fraud or wilful misconduct, or to amounts owed for services or goods actually delivered.

clauses.title: Indemnification
clauses.rationale: Who pays when a third party sues because of what one side did. Written mutually — a one-way indemnity is a negotiating position rather than a default.
clauses.body: Each party shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other, and its officers, employees, and agents, from any third-party claim, and from the resulting damages, losses, and reasonable legal costs, to the extent arising from the indemnifying party's breach of this {{thisDocument}}, negligence, or wilful misconduct. The party seeking indemnity shall notify the other promptly, allow it to control the defence, and cooperate reasonably. No settlement admitting fault or imposing an obligation on the indemnified party may be made without that party's consent.

clauses.title: Termination for Convenience
clauses.rationale: Either side can walk with notice. Worth being explicit that work already done still gets paid for.
clauses.body: Either party may terminate this {{thisDocument}} for [[termination for convenience|termination for convenience]] on thirty (30) days' written notice. On termination, the terminating party remains responsible for amounts due for work performed and expenses committed before the effective date of termination.

clauses.title: Termination for Cause
clauses.rationale: The cure period is what stops a minor slip becoming a termination right, and it is the part most often left out.
clauses.body: Either party may terminate this {{thisDocument}} if the other materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after written notice describing it. Either party may terminate immediately, without a cure period, if the other becomes insolvent, makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or has a receiver or trustee appointed over its assets.

clauses.title: Return of Property
clauses.rationale: Covers both information and physical property, because the end of a relationship usually involves some of each.
clauses.body: On termination of this {{thisDocument}} or on written request, each party shall return or destroy the other's confidential information, materials, equipment, and credentials in its possession, and shall confirm in writing that it has done so. A party may retain copies required by law or held in routine backup systems, which remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of this {{thisDocument}} for as long as they are retained.

clauses.title: Non-Solicitation of Personnel
clauses.rationale: Narrow by design: aimed at targeted poaching, not at ordinary hiring. The carve-outs for general advertising and for a person who approaches you first are what keep it from being a restraint on the individual, who is not a party to this document and did not agree to anything.
clauses.body: For twelve (12) months after this {{thisDocument}} ends, this [[non-solicitation|non-solicitation]] applies and neither party shall knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the other with whom it had material contact under this {{thisDocument}}. This does not restrict general advertising not targeted at that person, an approach initiated by the person, or the hiring of anyone whose employment has already ended. Enforceability of provisions of this kind varies considerably between jurisdictions; in some they are void.

clauses.title: Non-Compete
clauses.rationale: Included because the template library calls for it, and written as narrowly as the concept allows. This is the single most jurisdiction-dependent clause in the library — some states void it outright, others enforce it only if it is reasonable in time, geography and scope, and a few require separate consideration. The blanks are deliberate: a duration and a territory chosen by the user are more likely to be defensible than any default this tool could pick.
clauses.body: For [duration] after this {{thisDocument}} ends, the restricted party shall not, within [geographic area], engage in a business that directly competes with the specific business the other party carried on during the relationship. This restriction does not prevent passive ownership of less than one percent (1%) of a public company, nor employment in a role unrelated to the competing activity. Restrictions of this kind are unenforceable in some jurisdictions and are enforced elsewhere only so far as they are reasonable in duration, territory, and scope; consider taking advice before relying on this provision.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.rationale: The general-purpose version, for documents that do not carry their own. Five clauses in the corpus declare that they replace this one — the NDA's core obligations, the employment policy, the founder IP assignment, the contractor agreement and the MSA's incorporation by reference — because in those documents confidentiality is the subject rather than a boilerplate provision, and offering both would put two overlapping obligations in one document.
clauses.body: Each party shall hold the other's confidential information in confidence, use it only for the purposes of this {{thisDocument}}, and disclose it only to those of its personnel and advisors who need it and are bound by obligations at least as protective. Confidential information does not include information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving party, was known to it without restriction beforehand, is received from a third party free of any obligation of confidence, or is independently developed without reference to it. These obligations continue for three (3) years after this {{thisDocument}} ends, and indefinitely for anything that qualifies as a trade secret for as long as it remains one.
